newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS-Spread looks for rally in Gas.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS-Spread looks for rally in Gas.

text.p: A large bullish spread in British Gas options helped nudge the shares higher on Wednesday as old takeover rumours resurfaced in the market, dealers said.
The Evening Standard said there was speculation in the oil sector that Royal Dutch/Shell Group was considering an acquisition by year-end involving all or parts of British Gas.
Both companies declined to comment on the speculation.
But options dealers noted the sale of 1,000 December 180 puts at 2p against the purchase of 1,000 December 200 calls at 4p, a spread known in the options market as a "cylinder."
"It's almost a synthetic long. Someone probably wants to gain exposure in the stock, but those takeover rumours are about a year old," said one.
By 1439 GMT, 3,429 lots traded in British Gas options, with more than 2,050 lots trading in the December 280 calls.
British Gas shares were up 2-1/2p to 187-1/2p, off the day's high at 193-1/2p. They were among the most actively traded shares in London.
Dealers also noted the sale of a put spread in Shell options, whereby 550 January 950 puts were sold at 2p against the purchase of 550 January 1000 puts at 8p.
The spread will be profitable as long Shell shares, up 9p to 1059-1/2p, remain about 1000p, dealers said.

Options in Cable & Wireless were active again in the wake of the firm's merger, announced yesterday. Dealers said robust two-way business was seen with volatility levels still rising. More than 1,800 lots traded in C&W options.
C&W shares were up 4-1/2p to 471-1/2p, after having traded as high as 483p and as low as 467p earlier. They topped London's most active list with more than 13.6 million C&W shares trading hands.
